evals.name: pr-review-handoff-checking-mode
evals.prompt: We just finished a change in the repo at /work/billing-service on branch feature/BIL-401-invoice-rounding. It fixes a rounding bug where invoice line totals were rounded per-line before summing, so a 12-line invoice could be off by up to 6 cents against what the customer was quoted. We now sum in integer cents and round once at the end. 9 files changed, 3 commits, and I added a property test that generates random line sets and asserts the invoice total equals the quoted total. All 340 unit tests pass and the 22 integration tests pass. I also had to bump decimal.js from 10.4.3 to 10.5.0 because the old version had a subtle issue with toFixed on negatives, which matters for credit notes. PR is #114 on github.com/acme/billing-service, opened against develop. One gotcha we hit: the integration tests read fixtures from a generated /work/billing-service/.fixtures dir, and if you don't run `npm run fixtures:build` first they fail with a confusing ENOENT that looks like a code bug. I'm going to have a different session review this PR properly. Generate the prompt for that session.
evals.expected_output: A single paste-ready fenced code block containing a review prompt. It should identify checking mode explicitly to the user. It must name PR #114, the repo, and the branch. It must NOT assert that the fix is correct, that the tests pass as established fact the reviewer can rely on, or otherwise hand the reviewer conclusions to agree with; risk areas (the rounding change, the property test's actual strength, the dependency bump) should be phrased as questions for the reviewer to settle. It MUST include the fixtures:build trap with its confusing symptom, because that is an environment fact rather than a judgement.

evals.name: port-lint-rule-to-deployed-sibling-extending-mode
evals.prompt: The Biome config change is done and merged in ~/dev/catalog-api (commit a41f9c2 on main). We turned on the noFloatingPromises rule, fixed the 38 call sites it flagged, and learned a few things the hard way: the rule does not see promises returned through a `.then()` chain assigned to `void`, so those had to be rewritten as `await` inside a try/catch or the rule stays silent and the bug stays; `biome migrate` rewrites the config file and drops any comment in it, so we keep the reasoning in docs/adr/0007-floating-promises.md instead; and the pre-commit hook runs `biome check --staged` which passes on partially staged files even when the unstaged half breaks the rule, so the real gate is `npm run lint` on the whole tree. Now I want the same rule turned on in ~/dev/pricing-api. Difference: pricing-api is deployed to prod and its retry wrapper in src/lib/retry.ts relies on intentionally un-awaited fire-and-forget calls for metrics, so those need a `void` marker with a comment, not an await, or the request latency goes up. Write me a prompt to hand this to a fresh session.
evals.expected_output: A single paste-ready fenced code block. It should identify extending mode explicitly to the user, and therefore SHOULD state the established conclusions plainly (the `.then()` blind spot and the rewrite that fixes it, `biome migrate` dropping comments, the staged-only pre-commit gate and the real gate being `npm run lint`) rather than making the new session re-derive them. It must carry forward the pricing-api difference as the thing that changes the work: deployed to prod, and the fire-and-forget metrics calls in src/lib/retry.ts must be marked `void` with a comment rather than awaited. It should not withhold what was already learned, and it should not invent the number of call sites in pricing-api, the branch name, or a deployment procedure the user did not give.

evals.name: queue-consumer-verification-under-load-checking-mode
evals.prompt: I spent this session changing how our order-events consumer acknowledges messages (repo /srv/orders, file src/consumers/orderEvents.ts). It used to ack each RabbitMQ message on receipt and then process it, so a crash mid-processing lost the message. Now it processes first and acks after, with prefetch set to 50 and a redelivery cap of 3 before the message goes to the dead-letter queue. I believe this fixes the missing-orders reports from last month, and I believe prefetch 50 keeps throughput where it was, but I can't produce real load on my laptop. I want someone with access to the staging cluster to verify it under load rather than read my code. The replay tool is at /srv/tools/replay and you run it with `./replay --topic order-events --rate=N --duration=M`. Two things to know: staging's dead-letter queue is shared with the payments team, so anything you send there must be purged afterwards or their alerts fire; and the consumer's Prometheus counters reset every time the pod restarts, so a throughput number read across a restart is meaningless. Write a prompt I can give to whoever picks this up.
evals.expected_output: A single paste-ready fenced code block. Checking mode: the task is independent verification under load, so the prompt must not assert that the change fixes the missing-orders problem or that prefetch 50 preserves throughput; both beliefs are precisely what is being tested and should be framed as hypotheses to confirm or refute, with the receiving session told to settle them by its own measurement (for example, crash the consumer mid-processing during a replay, or compare throughput against a baseline it measures itself; any sound method counts) and never told what they settle to. It must include the replay invocation and both environment traps: the shared dead-letter queue that must be purged and the Prometheus counters that reset on pod restart. It should ask for evidence from the cluster rather than agreement, and it must not invent a baseline throughput number, an incident date beyond 'last month', or a list of changed files the user did not give.
